findings.title: No re-check of cache after taking the write lock
findings.body: When the cache is empty, several concurrent callers all see nil under the read lock and then queue on the write lock. Each then re-reads the manifest (file or CDN) in turn, because the cache is not re-checked once the lock is held. This is the classic check-lock-check mistake. Re-read entryPointAssetsCache after Lock() and return early if it is non-nil and cfg.Env != setting.Dev. Without that, the startup cache fill is serialized and redundant, and in Dev every request holds the exclusive lock during file I/O.

findings.title: Failed load overwrites a valid cache with nil
findings.body: On error, result is nil and the code still assigns entryPointAssetsCache = result. A transient failure, for example in Dev mode when the manifest is mid-rebuild, wipes a previously good cache. The function then returns (nil, err), and callers may dereference the nil pointer. Only update the cache when err == nil.
